Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession

| order by ConnCount desc

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Mail-borne click to fake FIFA World Cup 2026 phishing domain Delivery High
Detects users clicking links in email that resolve to known FIFA World Cup 2026 typosquat domains (fifa26.shop, *26-fifa.com and lookalike patterns). Pivots on Safe Links / email URL telemetry to catch the delivery vector before credential entry. Rationale: Uses the article's named IOC fifa26.shop plus the second sample family `*26-fifa[.]com`, expanded to a typosquat regex covering common .shop/.store TLDs the article explicitly calls out. Explicit allow for legitimate fifa.com prevents official-site collisions. Cross-checked: WHOIS/abuse.ch lookups for typosquat campaigns around major sporting events show recurring `<event>+<year>+.shop` patterns. Sentinel rewritten to use ImWebSession (EmailEvents/EmailUrlInfo are M365D-only and not in this tenant's Sentinel schema). Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/002/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1583/001/
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1583.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web Email.All_Email
let TyposquatRegex = @'(?i)(fifa.*(26|2026|worldcup)|(26|2026|worldcup).*fifa)';
let KnownBad = dynamic(['fifa26.shop','26-fifa.com']);
let ClickedUrls = UrlClickEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where ActionType in ('ClickAllowed','ClickedThrough','UrlScanInProgress')
  | where Url matches regex TyposquatRegex or parse_url(Url).Host has_any (KnownBad)
  | where not (Url matches regex @'(?i)://(www\.)?fifa\.com(/|$)');
ClickedUrls
| join kind=leftouter (EmailUrlInfo | where Timestamp > ago(7d) | project NetworkMessageId, UrlDomain, MailUrl=Url) on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, Url, MailUrl, UrlDomain, ActionType, ThreatTypes, NetworkMessageId, IPAddress, IsClickedThrough
| order by Timestamp desc
let TyposquatRegex = @'(?i)(fifa.*(26|2026|worldcup)|(26|2026|worldcup).*fifa)';
let KnownBad = dynamic(['fifa26.shop','26-fifa.com']);
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where isnotempty(Url)
| where Url matches regex TyposquatRegex or HttpHostName has_any (KnownBad)
| where not (Url matches regex @'(?i)://(www\.)?fifa\.com(/|$)') and not (HttpHostName endswith 'fifa.com')
| extend MailReferrer = iif(HttpRequestHeaderReferer matches regex @'(?i)(outlook|mail\.google|webmail|owa|m365|office\.com)', true, false)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, SrcHostname, DstHostname, Url, HttpHostName, HttpRequestHeaderReferer, MailReferrer, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Click or Navigation to Fake FIFA World Cup 2026 Typosquat Domain
id: 7c0e1f4a-8a6f-4f3d-9b1a-2f8c1d3e4b91
description: Detects browser navigation to known fake FIFA World Cup 2026 phishing domains and typosquat patterns reported by ESET.

[LLM] Endpoint DNS or web traffic to fake FIFA World Cup 2026 typosquat domain Delivery High
Detects endpoint DNS resolution or outbound web connection to fake FIFA World Cup 2026 phishing infrastructure (fifa26.shop, *26-fifa.com pattern) regardless of delivery vector — catches users reaching the site via sponsored search, social-media ads, or shared chat links. Rationale: Direct DNS/web pivot using the two domain families named in the article (fifa26.shop and *26-fifa.com), expanded to a tight typosquat regex bounded by the .shop/.store/.online TLDs the article specifically calls out as a red flag. Browser-process filter on the Defender side suppresses background DNS noise. Cross-checked against MITRE T1583.001 (typosquatting subtechnique). Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1583/001/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
ATT&CKT1566.003 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
let TyposquatRegex = @'(?i)(fifa.*(26|2026|worldcup)|(26|2026|worldcup).*fifa)\.(shop|store|online|xyz|top|site|com)';
let KnownBad = dynamic(['fifa26.shop','26-fifa.com']);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend Host = tolower(tostring(parse_url(RemoteUrl).Host))
| where Host has_any (KnownBad) or Host matches regex TyposquatRegex
| where not (Host endswith 'fifa.com') and Host != 'fifa.com'
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ('chrome.exe','msedge.exe','firefox.exe','brave.exe','opera.exe','iexplore.exe','safari.exe')
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteUrl, Host, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let TyposquatRegex = @'(?i)(fifa.*(26|2026|worldcup)|(26|2026|worldcup).*fifa)\.(shop|store|online|xyz|top|site|com)';
let KnownBad = dynamic(['fifa26.shop','26-fifa.com']);
union isfuzzy=true
  (DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where Name has_any (KnownBad) or Name matches regex TyposquatRegex
    | where not (Name endswith 'fifa.com') and Name != 'fifa.com'
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, QueryName=Name, QueryType=QueryTypeName, Result, Source='DnsEvents'),
  (ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DnsQuery has_any (KnownBad) or DnsQuery matches regex TyposquatRegex
    | where not (DnsQuery endswith 'fifa.com') and DnsQuery != 'fifa.com'
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, QueryName=DnsQuery, QueryType=DnsQueryTypeName, Result=DnsResponseName, Source='ImDnsActivity')
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Nx Console VS Code Extension Compromised
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Nx Console v18.95.0 Compromised VSIX / main.js / payload SHA-256 Hash Match · [LLM] macOS LaunchAgent Persistence — com.user.kitty-monitor.plist (Nx Console Compromise) · [LLM] Kitty cat.py Python Backdoor File Drop / Execution (Nx Console Compromise) · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] AWS IMDS (169.254.169.254) Hit from Developer / Non-EC2 Endpoint (Nx Console Credential Theft)
[LLM] Nx Console v18.95.0 Malicious Payload Bootstrap via Orphan Commit (npx github:nrwl/nx#558b09d7) Delivery High
Detects the malicious Nx Console v18.95.0 workspace-activation bootstrap step — npx (or node) executing code fetched from the dangling orphan commit 558b09d7 on github.com/nrwl/nx, spawned by a VS Code-family editor (Code, Code-Insiders, Cursor, Codium). This is the exact in-the-wild payload-fetch string published by StepSecurity. Rationale: The orphan-commit ref `558b09d7` (full SHA 558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2) and the `nrwl/nx#558b09d7` npx fragment are unique strings published in the StepSecurity report and confirmed by The Hacker News, GBHackers, and Cyberpress — no legitimate Nx workflow targets this hash. Parent constraint on VS Code-family editors anchors the workspace-activation behaviour described in the article. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html • https://gbhackers.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension/ • https://cyberpress.org/nx-console-hijacked-attack/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("code.exe","code - insiders.exe","cursor.exe","codium.exe","vscodium.exe","electron","code helper","code","cursor","codium")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("github:nrwl/nx#558b09d7","nrwl/nx#558b09d7","558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("\\Code.exe","\\Code - Insiders.exe","\\Cursor.exe","\\Codium.exe","\\VSCodium.exe")
    | where CommandLine has_any ("github:nrwl/nx#558b09d7","nrwl/nx#558b09d7","558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine),
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("code","cursor","codium","Code Helper","Code - Insiders","Electron")
    | where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("github:nrwl/nx#558b09d7","nrwl/nx#558b09d7","558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, Account = ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName = TargetProcessName, CommandLine = TargetProcessCommandLine)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Nx Console v18.95.0 Compromised VSIX / main.js / payload SHA-256 Hash Match Installation High
Detects file-system writes, process executions, or image loads matching any of the three SHA-256 hashes published by StepSecurity for the compromised Nx Console artefacts: the VSIX bundle, main.js, and the obfuscated index.js payload. Rationale: The three SHA-256 hashes are published verbatim in the StepSecurity post and corroborated by The Hacker News and GBHackers; a cryptographic hash match is the highest-fidelity primitive available. Hash collisions on SHA-256 are computationally infeasible — any hit on a non-sandbox host is a true positive. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html • https://gbhackers.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension/

[LLM] macOS LaunchAgent Persistence — com.user.kitty-monitor.plist (Nx Console Compromise) Installation High
Detects creation of the LaunchAgent plist `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.user.kitty-monitor.plist` — the macOS persistence mechanism dropped by the Nx Console v18.95.0 obfuscated payload to keep the credential-stealer running across logins. Rationale: The exact filename `com.user.kitty-monitor.plist` under `~/Library/LaunchAgents/` is published in the StepSecurity IOC list and corroborated by The Hacker News write-up. It is a unique persistence artefact — no legitimate macOS software uses this bundle identifier — making any file-create event on this path a true positive. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html • https://gbhackers.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension/
ATT&CKT1543.001 T1547
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has "/Library/LaunchAgents/" or FolderPath has @"\Library\LaunchAgents\"
| where FileName =~ "com.user.kitty-monitor.plist" or FolderPath endswith "com.user.kitty-monitor.plist"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","FileCreate")
| where TargetFilePath has "/Library/LaunchAgents/"
| where TargetFileName =~ "com.user.kitty-monitor.plist" or TargetFilePath endswith "com.user.kitty-monitor.plist"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, EventType, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Kitty cat.py Python Backdoor File Drop / Execution (Nx Console Compromise) Installation High
Detects creation of `~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py` or execution of a python interpreter referencing that path or `/tmp/kitty-*` — the Linux/macOS Python backdoor stage dropped by the Nx Console v18.95.0 obfuscated payload. Rationale: The path `~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py` and `/tmp/kitty-*` directories are published verbatim in the StepSecurity IOC list and corroborated by The Hacker News and GBHackers. The `kitty` directory under user-local share is unrelated to the legitimate Kitty terminal (which uses `~/.config/kitty/`) — there is no benign use of this exact path, making it high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html • https://gbhackers.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension/

[LLM] AWS IMDS (169.254.169.254) Hit from Developer / Non-EC2 Endpoint (Nx Console Credential Theft) Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects outbound connections to the AWS Instance Metadata Service (169.254.169.254) from endpoints that are not EC2 instances. The Nx Console v18.95.0 payload probes IMDS to steal IAM role credentials — a developer laptop or non-AWS workstation contacting IMDS is a strong credential-access signal. Rationale: The article and external corroboration (The Hacker News, CyberSecurityNews, GBHackers) call out `Connections to AWS IMDS (169.254.169.254) from non-AWS environments` as a documented IOC of the Nx Console payload's credential-stealing stage. The 169.254.169.254 link-local address has only one legitimate use (EC2/IMDS); any hit from a Mac/Linux laptop or developer workstation is anomalous. Sigma is omitted because the detection requires asset-class context (non-EC2) that single-event Sigma cannot express cleanly. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html • https://cybersecuritynews.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised/ • https://gbhackers.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension/
ATT&CKT1552.005 T1078.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
let DevEndpoints = DeviceInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, DeviceCategory, OSPlatform, DeviceType, IsInternetFacing) by DeviceId, DeviceName
    | where DeviceCategory != "Server" or isempty(DeviceCategory);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP == "169.254.169.254"
| where RemotePort in (80,443,8080)
| join kind=inner DevEndpoints on DeviceId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, OSPlatform, DeviceCategory, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr == "169.254.169.254"
| where DstPortNumber in (80,443,8080)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, SrcIpAddr, NetworkApplicationProtocol, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkBytes, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd OR source:linux.syslog OR source:osquery) (@DestinationIp:169.254.169.254 OR @network.destination.ip:169.254.169.254 OR @DestinationHostname:*169.254.169.254*) -@host.tags:cloud_provider\:aws
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemoteAddressIP4="169.254.169.254" RemotePort=/^(80|443|8080)$/ | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort], function=count())

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest

DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries Command & Control Medium
Long subdomain labels + frequent queries to a single 2LD = DNS C2/exfil.
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort == 53 and isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend qlen = strlen(RemoteUrl)
| where qlen > 50
| extend SecondLevelDomain = extract(@"([\w-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,})$", 1, RemoteUrl)
| summarize qcount = count(), uniqueSubs = dcount(RemoteUrl), maxLabel = max(qlen)
    by DeviceName, SecondLevelDomain
| where qcount > 100 and uniqueSubs > 20
| order by qcount desc
// ASIM ImDnsActivity normalises Windows DNS, Sysmon EID 22, Linux dnsmasq, etc.
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DnsQueryTypeName == "TXT"
| summarize Queries = count(), DistinctNames = dcount(DnsQuery)
            by SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Queries > 200    // tune to TXT-query baseline for environment
| order by Queries desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"

| eval qlen=len(query)

    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"

SecurityEvent

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1") or SHA1 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1") or MD5 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1") or SHA1 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1") or MD5 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__HASH_LIST__` placeholder with article-specific SHA256
    values. Use a watchlist or external indicator file for management
    at scale.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Hashes|contains:
            - 'SHA256=__HASH_PLACEHOLDER_REPLACE_ME__'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive hash match
level: critical
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.file_hash IN ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name, Filesystem.file_hash
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.process_hash IN ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process_hash
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`]

[LLM] OCI image extraction creates symlink with absolute path target (CWE-61 primitive) Exploitation High
Detects the Boxlite OCI layer extractor creating symlinks during tar processing where the link target points outside the staging directory (absolute path under /etc, /root, /home, /var/spool/cron, etc.). This is the core CVE-2026-46703 primitive — the unvalidated symlink target in apply_oci_layer() that turns a subsequent regular-file tar entry into an arbitrary host file write. Rationale: Article names the vulnerable binary explicitly (boxlite) and the exploit primitive's effect (writes outside dest staging dir into host paths like /etc/passwd, /root/.ssh/authorized_keys). The detection pivots on these two facts together — a high-fidelity pair because legitimate Boxlite extraction only writes inside its staging directory (typically /tmp/<sandbox-id>/ or /var/lib/boxlite/), never into /etc or /root. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f396-4rp4-7v2j
ATT&CKT1611 T1574 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "boxlite"
| where ActionType in~ ("FileCreated", "SymbolicLinkCreated")
| where FolderPath startswith "/etc/"
   or FolderPath startswith "/root/"
   or FolderPath startswith "/home/"
   or FolderPath startswith "/var/spool/cron/"
   or FolderPath startswith "/etc/cron.d/"
   or FolderPath startswith "/etc/sudoers.d/"
   or FolderPath startswith "/etc/systemd/system/"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where SyslogMessage has "boxlite"
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("symlink", "symlinkat", "linkat")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("/etc/", "/root/", "/home/", "/var/spool/cron", "/etc/cron.d", "/etc/sudoers.d", "/etc/systemd/system")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProcessName, ProcessID, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Boxlite sandbox writes to SSH authorized_keys (post-exploit RCE pivot) Installation High
Detects the Boxlite service writing to any authorized_keys file on the host — the article explicitly calls out this technique as the RCE pivot ('writing the attacker's public key into the host's authorized_keys'). Since Boxlite has no legitimate reason to touch user SSH key files outside its sandboxed Box filesystems, any such write is high-confidence post-exploitation of CVE-2026-46703. Rationale: Article body explicitly cites this technique: 'The attacker can further leverage this capability to achieve remote code execution, such as writing the attacker's public key into the host's authorized_keys.' Boxlite is a container sandbox — it has zero legitimate workflow that involves writing to /root/.ssh/ or /home/*/.ssh/ on the host, making this a clean alerting signal. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f396-4rp4-7v2j

[LLM] Vulnerable Twig package (CVE-2026-46633) installed (twig/twig < 3.26.0) Exploitation High
Surface assets where Microsoft Defender TVM reports the Twig PHP templating library at a version vulnerable to CVE-2026-46633. Exploitation gives RCE via single-quote injection in a `{% use %}` template name; SecurityPolicy allows `{% use %}` even under sandbox, so any application that accepts attacker-influenced template names against twig/twig < 3.26.0 is reachable. Prioritise patching to 3.26.0 or later. Rationale: Article is a vendor advisory: identifies the exact package (composer:twig/twig), fixed version (3.26.0), and CVE (CVE-2026-46633). The only high-fidelity, non-generic detection from this content is asset coverage — every other behaviour-based UC (PHP web server spawning shells, web-shell cache file writes) collapses into generic web-shell rules already shipped, which the prompt explicitly excludes. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7p85-w9px-jpjp

[LLM] AWS IAM role trust policy created with set-qualified operator on GitHub OIDC sub claim Installation High
Hunts the exact misconfiguration class that @hulumi/policies <1.3.2 failed to flag: CreateRole/UpdateAssumeRolePolicy CloudTrail events whose trust policy uses ForAnyValue:StringLike / ForAllValues:StringLike / ForAllValues:StringEquals against token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub. Any role created with this shape — particularly with wildcards in the sub value — is assumable by GitHub Actions workflows the role owner never intended to authorize. Rationale: Article specifies the exact unsafe pattern: set-qualified operators (ForAnyValue:StringLike etc.) applied to token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub bypass the inspector. CloudTrail's CreateRole/UpdateAssumeRolePolicy carries the full policyDocument as JSON — substring matching for both the operator family AND the OIDC sub claim string is high-fidelity because the combination is essentially never seen in correctly-authored trust policies (canonical pattern is the bare StringLike or StringEquals). Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/avoiding-mistakes-with-aws-oidc-integration-conditions • https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_elements_condition_operators.html • https://docs.github.com/en/actions/deployment/security-hardening-your-deployments/configuring-openid-connect-in-amazon-web-services
ATT&CKT1098.003 T1199 T1078.004

[LLM] AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity from GitHub OIDC with unexpected repo/branch sub claim Exploitation Medium
Downstream hunt for actor abuse of a role whose unsafe trust policy slipped past @hulumi/policies <1.3.2. Pivots on sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity events where the WebIdentity issuer is token.actions.githubusercontent.com and the asserted sub claim does not match the org's approved GitHub repo allowlist — flagging the first-time-seen repo+role pairs that an attacker exploiting a wildcard sub policy would generate. Rationale: The article's bypass directly enables GitHub Actions OIDC sub-claim impersonation against IAM roles. AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity is the actor-observable consequence — the userIdentity.userName field on the CloudTrail event carries the asserted sub (e.g. repo:owner/repo:ref:refs/heads/main). Anti-joining against an approved-org/repo lookup is the cleanest baseline-deviation pivot for catching exploitation of an unsafe policy that the scanner missed. Cross-referenced with the AWS GitHub OIDC docs and the Wiz misconfiguration write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/avoiding-mistakes-with-aws-oidc-integration-conditions • https://docs.github.com/en/actions/deployment/security-hardening-your-deployments/configuring-openid-connect-in-amazon-web-services

[LLM] CVE-2026-46614: Unauthorized /fission-function/ invocation on Fission router public listener (port 8888) Exploitation High
Detects HTTP requests to the internal-style /fission-function/<ns>/<name> route on the Fission router's public listener (svc/router, port 8888). On versions <= 1.22.0 this route is mounted on the public listener and allows any caller reaching the router to invoke any Function object — bypassing HTTPTrigger host/path/method restrictions. Post-fix (v1.23.0+), this path should only exist on port 8889 (svc/router-internal, ClusterIP-only), so any hit on port 8888 is either an unpatched cluster being exploited or an enumeration probe. Rationale: The path string `/fission-function/` and port 8888 are both directly named in the GHSA advisory as the vulnerable surface (pkg/router/httpTriggers.go:280-284 and svc/router listener config). After v1.23.0 this path should only appear on port 8889 (svc/router-internal), so hits on 8888 are unambiguous - either an exploitation attempt or an unpatched cluster still serving the route. We exclude 404 because that's enumeration covered by the next UC; 200 means successful unauthorized invocation, 502 means the function exists and went cold (still a successful enumeration). Defender KQL is empty because Fission runs on Linux K8s nodes and the relevant telemetry is HTTP-layer (ingress/WAF), not endpoint EDR. Falcon LogScale is empty for the same reason - FDR doesn't ship ingress HTTP path data. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/fission/fission/releases/tag/v1.23.0 • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3g33-6vg6-27m8
ATT&CKT1190 T1133
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Fission runs on Kubernetes (Linux) - this detection lives in ingress/WAF logs forwarded to CommonSecurityLog or web-tier IIS logs in front of the router
union isfuzzy=true
(
  CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestURL has "/fission-function/"
  | where DestinationPort == 8888 or isempty(tostring(DestinationPort))
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestMethod, RequestURL, EventOutcome, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, RequestClientApplication
  | extend Verdict = case(EventOutcome has "200", "Successful unauthorized invocation", EventOutcome has "502", "Cold-start - function exists", EventOutcome has "404", "Probe miss", "Other - verify")
),
(
  W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csUriStem has "/fission-function/"
  | where sPort == 8888
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP=cIP, DestinationIP=Computer, DestinationPort=sPort, RequestMethod=csMethod, RequestURL=strcat(csUriStem, iff(isnotempty(csUriQuery), strcat("?",csUriQuery), "")), EventOutcome=tostring(scStatus), DeviceVendor="Microsoft", DeviceProduct="IIS", RequestClientApplication=csUserAgent
  | extend Verdict = case(EventOutcome == "200", "Successful unauthorized invocation", EventOutcome == "502", "Cold-start - function exists", EventOutcome == "404", "Probe miss", "Other - verify")
)
| where Verdict != "Probe miss"   // 200/502 = signal; 404 alone is enumeration noise covered by UC2
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Fission Function Name Enumeration via /fission-function/ Probing (CVE-2026-46614 recon) Reconnaissance Medium
Detects function-name discovery against the Fission router by counting distinct /fission-function/<ns>/<name> paths probed from the same source within a short window. Per the advisory, callers can enumerate which functions exist by differentiating response semantics (404 = no such function, 200 = invoked, 502 = function exists and went cold). A burst of 404s interleaved with 200/502s from one source is the canonical recon shape. Rationale: The advisory explicitly calls out enumeration as an impact: 'Enumerate function names by probing the response semantics (404 vs 200 vs 502 from cold start).' Counting distinct paths under /fission-function/ per source IP in a short window directly models that pattern; requiring at least 3 404s alongside the path-count threshold filters legitimate trigger callers (who hit known paths and don't miss). Sigma is empty because this is a count/threshold detection, not single-event-shape. Defender and Falcon are empty because the telemetry sits at the ingress/WAF layer, not on endpoints. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/fission/fission/releases/tag/v1.23.0 • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3g33-6vg6-27m8
ATT&CKT1595.003 T1083
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let LookbackHours = 24h;
let WindowMinutes = 10m;
let MinUniquePaths = 5;
let MinProbeMisses = 3;
union isfuzzy=true
(
  CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
  | where RequestURL has "/fission-function/"
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, RequestURL, Status=tostring(EventOutcome), UserAgent=RequestClientApplication, Router=DestinationIP
),
(
  W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
  | where csUriStem has "/fission-function/"
  | where sPort == 8888
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP=cIP, RequestURL=csUriStem, Status=tostring(scStatus), UserAgent=csUserAgent, Router=Computer
)
| summarize
    UniqueFunctionPaths = dcount(RequestURL),
    TotalRequests = count(),
    HitFunctions = dcountif(RequestURL, Status in ("200","502")),
    MissFunctions = dcountif(RequestURL, Status == "404"),
    SamplePaths = make_set(RequestURL, 20),
    UserAgents = make_set(UserAgent, 5),
    Routers = make_set(Router, 3)
    by bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMinutes), SourceIP
| where UniqueFunctionPaths >= MinUniquePaths and MissFunctions >= MinProbeMisses
| extend EnumerationConfidence = case(
    HitFunctions > 0 and MissFunctions >= 3, "High - mixed 200/502 hits with 404 misses (likely successful enumeration)",
    MissFunctions >= 10, "Medium - heavy 404 probing",
    "Low")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
(source:nginx OR source:kubernetes) @http.url_details.path:*/fission-function/*

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| where UniqueFunctionPaths >= 5 AND MissFunctions >= 3
| eval EnumerationConfidence=case(HitFunctions>0 AND MissFunctions>=3,"High - mixed 200/502 hits with 404 misses",MissFunctions>=10,"Medium - heavy 404 probing",true(),"Low")
| table _time, src, UniqueFunctionPaths, TotalRequests, HitFunctions, MissFunctions, EnumerationConfidence, Routers, UserAgents
| tstats summariesonly=false dc(Web.url) as UniqueFunctionPaths, count as TotalRequests, dc(eval(if(Web.status=="200" OR Web.status=="502", Web.url, null()))) as HitFunctions, dc(eval(if(Web.status=="404", Web.url, null()))) as MissFunctions, values(Web.http_user_agent) as UserAgents, values(Web.dest) as Routers from datamodel=Web where Web.url="*/fission-function/*" by _time span=10m, Web.src

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).

[LLM] BadIIS rogue native module drop in IIS folders (demo.pdb / Chinese path heuristic) Installation Medium
Hunts non-trusted writes of DLL/native modules into IIS-served directories (\inetsrv\, \inetpub\wwwroot\bin\), and image loads by w3wp.exe of modules outside the canonical IIS install paths or whose file path contains Han/CJK characters. Targets the Talos-described BadIIS commodity variant whose modules carry 'demo.pdb' strings and Chinese-language folder paths. Rationale: Article explicitly names 'demo.pdb' strings and Chinese-language folder paths inside IIS binaries as the Talos-recommended hunt hooks. Standard EDR can't search PDB strings inline, so we proxy with (a) writes of native modules into IIS paths by non-installer processes and (b) the CJK Unicode range (\u4e00-\u9fff) in module paths, which catches the Chinese-folder-path signal directly. Memory mem-1304 already corroborated BadIIS as commodity MaaS infrastructure.
ATT&CKT1505.004 T1036.005

description: Detects file writes of DLL or EXE payloads into IIS-served directories (\inetsrv\, \inetpub\wwwroot\bin\) by a process that is NOT msiexec / TrustedInstaller / appcmd / drvinst. Aligns with Cisco Talos BadIIS commodity variant (May 2026) whose modules drop into IIS module paths and carry 'demo.pdb' strings.

[LLM] Talos weekly prevalent-malware hash hit (Coinminer worm / TunMirror / SECOH-QAD / KMS-Loader) Installation High
Hash IOC sweep for the five Talos-published prevalent-malware SHA256s for the week ending May 21 2026: Win.Worm.Coinminer (VID001.exe), PUA.Win.Tool.Tunmirror (TunMirror.exe), Win.Tool.Procpatcher (SECOH-QAD.exe), and the KM-prefixed sample. Covers process execution, file writes, and DLL/EXE module loads to surface infection regardless of stage. Rationale: Direct hash IOCs published by Cisco Talos with detection name + sample filename per hash. These are the week's top prevalent samples — VID001.exe (Coinminer worm), TunMirror.exe (network tunneling PUA), SECOH-QAD.exe (KMS-emulation tooling), KM-prefix loader. Hash equality is the highest-fidelity detection shape possible. [LLM] BadIIS traffic-hijacking: IIS 503 surge + anomalous external redirect ratio per site/hour Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the Talos-described BadIIS impact pattern: hijacked IIS servers throwing 503 spikes (proxy/upstream failure) while also emitting an unusually high ratio of 30x/redirect responses pointing visitors to attacker-controlled SEO-fraud destinations. Aggregates per site per hour and flags hours that materially deviate from the per-site baseline. Rationale: Article explicitly tells defenders to 'actively monitor IIS environments for unauthorized traffic redirection, unexpected reverse proxying, or sudden spikes in 503 Service Unavailable errors' — this query is a direct expression of that guidance, anchored on per-site/per-hour anomalies versus a 30-day baseline so it doesn't fire on legitimately redirect-heavy sites. Datadog and Falcon LogScale fields left empty because raw IIS W3C access logs are not part of the standard FDR feed and are not in the Datadog source list provided.
ATT&CKT1496 T1565.002 T1090
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let lookback = 7d;
let bucket = 1h;
let BadIISSignals = W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where csMethod in~ ("GET","HEAD","POST")
| summarize Total = count(),
           Status503 = countif(scStatus == 503),
           Status3xx = countif(scStatus between (300 .. 399)),
           DistinctClients = dcount(cIP),
           DistinctURIs = dcount(csUriStem),
           SampleUserAgents = make_set(csUserAgent, 5),
           SampleReferers = make_set(csReferer, 5)
           by Computer, sSiteName, bin(TimeGenerated, bucket)
| extend PctErr503 = round((Status503 * 100.0) / Total, 2),
         PctRedirect = round((Status3xx * 100.0) / Total, 2)
| where (Status503 >= 50 and PctErr503 >= 20) or (Status3xx >= 100 and PctRedirect >= 40);
let Baseline = W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated between (ago(30d) .. ago(lookback))
| summarize BaselineTotal = count(),
           BaselineRedirect = countif(scStatus between (300 .. 399)),
           Baseline503 = countif(scStatus == 503)
           by Computer, sSiteName
| extend BaselinePctRedirect = round((BaselineRedirect * 100.0) / BaselineTotal, 2),
         BaselinePctErr503 = round((Baseline503 * 100.0) / BaselineTotal, 2);
BadIISSignals
| join kind=leftouter Baseline on Computer, sSiteName
| where PctRedirect >= (coalesce(BaselinePctRedirect, 0.0) * 3) or PctErr503 >= (coalesce(BaselinePctErr503, 0.0) * 3)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, sSiteName, Total, Status503, Status3xx, PctErr503, PctRedirect, BaselinePctRedirect, BaselinePctErr503, DistinctClients, DistinctURIs, SampleUserAgents, SampleReferers
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] npm/node lifecycle script fetching Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun Installation High
Detects an npm preinstall/postinstall lifecycle script (node.exe parented by npm) reaching out to github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases to download the Bun v1.3.13 runtime. This is the exact bootstrap behaviour of the TeamPCP @bitwarden/cli@2026.4.0 payload (bw_setup.js Stage-1) and is highly anomalous on developer endpoints because legitimate JS projects rarely pull Bun via a package-install hook. Rationale: Article explicitly names github.com/oven-sh/bun and Bun v1.3.13 as the runtime downloaded by Stage-1 bw_setup.js during npm preinstall — pairing the github.com/oven-sh/bun URL token with an npm-family parent process is a near-zero-FP signature on production endpoints (developer laptops will produce occasional FPs, hence the parent-process pinning). Cross-checked against Socket and Checkmarx advisories listed below. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/teampcp-bitwarden-cli-supply-chain • https://checkmarx.com/blog/checkmarx-supply-chain-incident-april-2026/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let bunUrlIndicators = dynamic(["github.com/oven-sh/bun", "oven-sh/bun/releases", "bun-windows-x64", "bun-linux-x64", "bun-darwin"]);
let npmParents = dynamic(["npm.exe","npm-cli.js","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe"]);
let downloaderChildren = dynamic(["node.exe","curl.exe","powershell.exe","wget.exe","bun.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","pwsh.exe"]);
// Process-tree pivot — npm parent spawning a downloader child with Bun URL on the command line
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (npmParents) or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (npmParents)
    | where FileName in~ (downloaderChildren)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (bunUrlIndicators) or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (bunUrlIndicators)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
              InitImage  = InitiatingProcessFileName,
              InitCmd    = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              ChildImage = FileName,
              ChildCmd   = ProcessCommandLine, SHA256;
// Network pivot — same process families connecting to github.com for the Bun release tarball
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where RemoteUrl has "github.com" and (RemoteUrl has "oven-sh/bun" or RemoteUrl has "bun-windows" or RemoteUrl has "bun-linux" or RemoteUrl has "bun-darwin")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (downloaderChildren)
    | where InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (npmParents) or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (npmParents)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName,
              AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
              InitImage   = InitiatingProcessFileName,
              InitCmd     = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,

let bunUrlIndicators = dynamic(["github.com/oven-sh/bun", "oven-sh/bun/releases", "bun-windows-x64", "bun-linux-x64", "bun-darwin"]);

title: NPM Lifecycle Script Downloading Bun Runtime from oven-sh GitHub
id: 4c2f6f8a-9d1e-4b8c-9a3f-2e8a0b1c4d51
status: experimental
description: Detects an npm/yarn/pnpm install lifecycle script (Node.js parented by npm) spawning a downloader to fetch the Bun JavaScript runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun — the Stage-1 bootstrap of the TeamPCP @bitwarden/cli supply-chain payload.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/monitoring-npm-supply-chain-attacks/
  - https://socket.dev/blog/teampcp-bitwarden-cli-supply-chain
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.007
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'
      - '\npx.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
      - '\bun.exe'
  selection_url:

      - 'bun-windows-x64'

      - 'bun-darwin'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_url
falsepositives:
  - Developer manually upgrading the Bun runtime via an automation script
  - CI agent installing Bun in a build pipeline (scope detection to dev workstations or scope out CI hosts)
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\npm.exe OR *\NPM.exe OR *\node.exe OR *\NODE.exe OR *\yarn.exe OR *\pnpm.exe OR *\npx.exe) @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\NODE.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\CURL.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\wget.exe OR *\bun.exe) @CommandLine:(*github.com/oven-sh/bun* OR *oven-sh/bun/releases* OR *bun-windows-x64* OR *bun-linux-x64* OR *bun-darwin*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(npm|node|yarn|pnpm|npx)(\.exe)?$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(node|curl|powershell|pwsh|wget|bun|bash|sh)\.exe$/i
| regex("github\.com/oven-sh/bun|oven-sh/bun/releases|bun-(windows|linux|darwin)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

[LLM] C2 beacon to audit.checkmarx[.]cx /v1/telemetry (TeamPCP Shai-Hulud Third Coming) Command & Control High
Detects any outbound network/DNS activity to the TeamPCP C2 audit.checkmarx[.]cx (94.154.172.43) — particularly POSTs to the /v1/telemetry path — that exfiltrates harvested cloud, CI/CD and developer credentials from compromised hosts. The domain visually impersonates Checkmarx's legitimate infrastructure but resolves to attacker-controlled space. Rationale: Article Table 1 names the C2 server, IP and HTTP path explicitly (audit.checkmarx[.]cx:443 / 94.154.172.43 / /v1/telemetry) — any hit on these three indicators is a confirmed-compromise signal, not a hunting hypothesis. Corroborated by Checkmarx's official disclosure that all four artifact families (npm, Docker Hub, GitHub Actions, VS Code) shared this C2. Cross-checked against: • https://checkmarx.com/blog/checkmarx-supply-chain-incident-april-2026/ • https://socket.dev/blog/teampcp-bitwarden-cli-supply-chain
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
let c2Hosts = dynamic(["audit.checkmarx.cx", "audit.checkmarx[.]cx"]);
let c2Ips    = dynamic(["94.154.172.43"]);
let c2Path   = "/v1/telemetry";
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (RemoteUrl has_any (c2Hosts)) or (RemoteIP in (c2Ips)) or (RemoteUrl has c2Path and RemotePort in (443, 80))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","SenseIR.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName,
          AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let c2Hosts = dynamic(["audit.checkmarx.cx"]);
let c2Ips    = dynamic(["94.154.172.43"]);
let c2Path   = "/v1/telemetry";
union isfuzzy=true
(
  ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DstHostname has_any (c2Hosts) or DstIpAddr in (c2Ips) or (isnotempty(Url) and Url has c2Path and DstPortNumber in (443, 80))
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkApplicationProtocol
),
(
  ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any (c2Hosts)
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DnsQuery, DnsQueryTypeName, DnsResponseCodeName
),
(
  ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where HttpHostName has_any (c2Hosts) or Url has c2Path and (HttpHostName has "checkmarx.cx")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, HttpHostName, Url, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode
),
(
  CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DestinationHostName has_any (c2Hosts) or DestinationIP in (c2Ips) or RequestURL has "audit.checkmarx.cx" or RequestURL has c2Path
  | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, SourceIP, SourceHostName, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, RequestMethod
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: TeamPCP Shai-Hulud C2 audit.checkmarx[.]cx Connection
id: 7e5a3b2c-1f4d-4a6e-9b8f-3c2d1e4f5a62
status: experimental
description: Detects connections or DNS resolutions to the TeamPCP / Shai-Hulud Third Coming C2 infrastructure (audit.checkmarx[.]cx / 94.154.172.43) used by the @bitwarden/cli@2026.4.0 npm supply-chain payload and the broader Checkmarx-distribution-channel compromise to exfiltrate harvested credentials via /v1/telemetry.

[LLM] Malicious @bitwarden/cli payload artifacts on disk (bw_setup.js, bw1.js, Shai-Hulud markers) Installation High
Detects creation or execution of the Stage-1 (bw_setup.js) and Stage-2 (bw1.js) Node.js scripts dropped by the TeamPCP @bitwarden/cli@2026.4.0 npm package, as well as the 'Shai-Hulud: The Third Coming' string written into public repo content that the worm uses as an attribution marker and propagation beacon. This catches both the install-time drop on the npm install path and any post-compromise replay. Rationale: Article explicitly names bw_setup.js (Stage-1 bootstrap, registered as the `bw` bin) and bw1.js (Stage-2 Bun payload) inside the malicious @bitwarden/cli@2026.4.0 package. The legitimate Bitwarden CLI ships neither filename, so the filename + package path combo is a hard-IOC match. The Shai-Hulud Third Coming string is a TeamPCP attribution marker per the article body. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/teampcp-bitwarden-cli-supply-chain • https://github.com/bitwarden/clients/security/advisories
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1546.016 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
let stageFiles = dynamic(["bw_setup.js", "bw1.js"]);
let packageHints = dynamic(["@bitwarden\\cli", "@bitwarden/cli", "node_modules\\@bitwarden\\cli", "node_modules/@bitwarden/cli"]);
let shaiHuludMarker = "Shai-Hulud: The Third Coming";
let FileHits = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where (FileName in~ (stageFiles)) or (FolderPath has_any (packageHints) and FileName endswith ".js") or (AdditionalFields has shaiHuludMarker)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName,
              AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
              FolderPath, FileName, SHA256;
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npm-cli.js","bun.exe")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (stageFiles)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
              FolderPath, FileName = FileName, SHA256, ProcCmd = ProcessCommandLine;
union FileHits, ProcHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let stageFiles = dynamic(["bw_setup.js", "bw1.js"]);
let packageHints = dynamic(["@bitwarden\\cli", "@bitwarden/cli", "node_modules\\@bitwarden\\cli", "node_modules/@bitwarden/cli"]);
let npmRunners = dynamic(["npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npm-cli.js","bun.exe","npm","node","yarn","pnpm","bun"]);
let FileHits = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where (TargetFileName in~ (stageFiles)) or (TargetFilePath has_any (packageHints) and TargetFileExtension =~ "js")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
              ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
              TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256;
let ProcHits = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ActingProcessName has_any (npmRunners) or ParentProcessName has_any (npmRunners)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (stageFiles)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
              ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
              ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
              TargetFilePath = "", TargetFileName = "", TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256;
union FileHits, ProcHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType
