title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99") or SHA1 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99") or MD5 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99") or SHA1 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99") or MD5 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b
status: experimental

ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.file_hash IN ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name, Filesystem.file_hash
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("timeago.js"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)

| where (FileName in~ ("timeago.js"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

Microsoft Takes Down Malware-Signing Service Behind Ransomware Attacks

The Hacker News
2026-05-20 13 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Microsoft on Tuesday said it disrupted a malware-signing-as-a-service (MSaaS) operation that weaponized the company's Artifact Signing system to deliver malicious code and conduct ransomware and other attacks, compromising thousands of machines and networks across the world. The tech giant attributed the activity to a threat actor it calls Fox Tempest, which it said offered the MSaaS scheme

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Search-ad delivery of fake Microsoft Teams/AnyDesk/PuTTY/Webex installers · Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Hunt for SignSpace-signed binaries via Fox Tempest IOC hashes · [LLM] Oyster loader execution via SignSpace-signed Teams/AnyDesk impersonator · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Beaconing or DNS resolution to signspace.cloud / Fox Tempest infrastructure · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Rhysida ransomware deployment downstream of SignSpace-signed installer · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] Hunt for SignSpace-signed binaries via Fox Tempest IOC hashes Installation High
Surfaces any execution, file write or image load whose SHA256/SHA1 matches the Microsoft DCU IOC bundle published for the OpFauxSign / SignSpace operation. This is a direct hash hunt against the binaries Fox Tempest signed and shipped to ransomware affiliates (Vanilla Tempest, INC, Qilin, BlackByte, Akira). Rationale: Hashes drawn directly from the pre-extracted IOC block (SHA256/SHA1) published with the Microsoft DCU disclosure of OpFauxSign. Multi-table union covers execution, write-to-disk, and DLL load so a payload dropped but not yet run is still surfaced. Cross-checked against: • https://blogs.microsoft.com/on-the-issues/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1553/002/
ATT&CKT1553.002 T1036.001 T1036.005

[LLM] Search-ad delivery of fake Microsoft Teams/AnyDesk/PuTTY/Webex installers Delivery Medium
Detects browser-driven downloads of brand-impersonating installers (Teams, AnyDesk, PuTTY, Webex) from non-canonical domains following click on a sponsored search-result. Mirrors the Vanilla Tempest TTP of paid Google ads redirecting Teams-seekers to attacker-hosted SignSpace-signed payloads. Rationale: Anchors on the exact four brands the article names — Microsoft Teams, AnyDesk, PuTTY, Cisco Webex — combined with the malvertising delivery shape (browser-spawned write of brand-named installer to Downloads/Temp from a non-canonical host). FileOriginUrl is the key pivot that distinguishes a legitimate download from a search-ad redirect. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1583/008/ • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-devicefileevents-table
ATT&CKT1583.008 T1608.006 T1189
Data sourcesWeb.Web Endpoint.Filesystem

let TrustedDownloadHosts = dynamic(["microsoft.com","teams.microsoft.com","statics.teams.cdn.office.net","anydesk.com","download.anydesk.com","chiark.greenend.org.uk","the.earth.li","webex.com","binaries.webex.com","cisco.com"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| where tolower(FileName) in (LureNames)
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\")
| extend OriginHost = tolower(tostring(parse_url(FileOriginUrl).Host))
| where isnotempty(OriginHost)
| where not (OriginHost has_any (TrustedDownloadHosts))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, FileOriginUrl, FileOriginReferrerUrl, OriginHost, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] Oyster loader execution via SignSpace-signed Teams/AnyDesk impersonator Installation High
Detects the post-execution behaviour of Oyster (aka Broomstick / CleanUpLoader) when delivered through a SignSpace-signed installer: a brand-named installer launches rundll32.exe / regsvr32.exe to side-load a non-Microsoft DLL, and creates a scheduled task for persistence. Targets the article-specific delivery → execution chain. Rationale: Pivots on the article-specific parent (brand-impersonating signed installer in Downloads/Temp) and the documented Oyster loader behaviour (rundll32 side-load, schtasks persistence). Excludes the noisy bare LOLBin-execution shape by demanding the brand-named parent dropped in a user-writable path. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/002/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/ • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/2024/06/17/malvertising-campaign-leads-to-execution-of-oyster-backdoor/
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1574.002 T1053.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let LureParents = dynamic(["teams_setup.exe","teamssetup.exe","msteams-x64.exe","msteams_setup.exe","anydesk.exe","anydesksetup.exe","putty.exe","puttysetup.exe","webex.msi","webexapp.msi","ciscowebexsetup.exe","webexsetup.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where tolower(InitiatingProcessFileName) in (LureParents)
| where FileName in~ ("rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","schtasks.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","msiexec.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\")
| extend SuspiciousArg = case(
    FileName =~ "rundll32.exe" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\\(AppData|ProgramData|Users\\Public)\\.*\.dll", "rundll32-userdll",
    FileName =~ "regsvr32.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/s","/i:"), "regsvr32-silent",
    FileName =~ "schtasks.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/create","/CREATE"), "schtasks-create",
    FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-w hidden","-WindowStyle Hidden","-enc","DownloadString","IEX"), "ps-obfuscated",
    "other")
| where SuspiciousArg != "other"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ParentFile=InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentFolder=InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ParentSHA256=InitiatingProcessSHA256, ChildFile=FileName, ChildCmd=ProcessCommandLine, SuspiciousArg
| order by Timestamp desc
let LureParents = dynamic(["teams_setup.exe","teamssetup.exe","msteams-x64.exe","msteams_setup.exe","anydesk.exe","anydesksetup.exe","putty.exe","puttysetup.exe","webex.msi","webexapp.msi","ciscowebexsetup.exe","webexsetup.exe"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(ImProcessCreate
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
 | where tolower(ParentProcessName) in (LureParents)
 | where TargetProcessName has_any ("rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","schtasks.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","msiexec.exe")
 | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, User=ActorUsername, Parent=ParentProcessName, ParentCmd=ParentProcessCommandLine, Child=TargetProcessName, ChildCmd=TargetProcessCommandLine),
(SecurityEvent
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
 | where EventID == 4688
 | extend ParentFile = tolower(tostring(split(ParentProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
 | where ParentFile in (LureParents)
 | extend ChildFile = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
 | where ChildFile in ("rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","schtasks.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","msiexec.exe")
 | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, User=Account, Parent=ParentProcessName, ParentCmd="", Child=NewProcessName, ChildCmd=CommandLine)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Oyster Loader Child Process via SignSpace-Signed Brand Installer

[LLM] Beaconing or DNS resolution to signspace.cloud / Fox Tempest infrastructure Command & Control High
Detects any process- or proxy-initiated DNS lookup, web request or network connection referencing signspace.cloud — Microsoft DCU's named Fox Tempest C2/operator domain seized under OpFauxSign. Even post-seizure, residual lookups from compromised hosts indicate prior installation of a SignSpace-signed payload. Rationale: signspace.cloud is the only named operator domain in the Microsoft DCU disclosure and is hard-coded in the article + IOC block. Single-domain hash, so high-fidelity. Sentinel_kql fixed to use DnsEvents.Name/Question, ImDnsActivity.DnsQuery, ImWebSession.HttpHostName, CommonSecurityLog.DestinationHostName — all valid columns on their respective tables. Cross-checked against: • https://blogs.microsoft.com/on-the-issues/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let SuspiciousDomains = dynamic(["signspace.cloud"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(DeviceNetworkEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
 | where RemoteUrl has_any (SuspiciousDomains) or RemoteUrl endswith ".signspace.cloud"
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol, Source="DeviceNetworkEvents"),
(DeviceEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
 | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
 | where RemoteUrl has_any (SuspiciousDomains) or AdditionalFields has "signspace.cloud"
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP=tostring(RemoteIP), RemotePort=tostring(RemotePort), Protocol="DNS", Source="DeviceEvents-DNS")
| order by Timestamp desc
let SuspiciousDomains = dynamic(["signspace.cloud"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
 | where Name has_any (SuspiciousDomains) or Question has_any (SuspiciousDomains)
 | project TimeGenerated, SourceHost=Computer, SourceIP=ClientIP, Query=Name, QueryType=QueryTypeName, Resolved=Result, Table="DnsEvents"),
(ImDnsActivity
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
 | where DnsQuery has_any (SuspiciousDomains) or DnsQueryName has_any (SuspiciousDomains)
 | project TimeGenerated, SourceHost=DvcHostname, SourceIP=SrcIpAddr, Query=DnsQuery, QueryType=DnsQueryTypeName, Resolved=DnsResponseName, Table="ImDnsActivity"),
(ImWebSession
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
 | where HttpHostName has_any (SuspiciousDomains) or Url has_any (SuspiciousDomains)
 | project TimeGenerated, SourceHost=SrcHostname, SourceIP=SrcIpAddr, Query=Url, QueryType="HTTP", Resolved=DstHostname, Table="ImWebSession"),
(CommonSecurityLog
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
 | where DestinationHostName has_any (SuspiciousDomains) or RequestURL has_any (SuspiciousDomains)
 | project TimeGenerated, SourceHost=SourceHostName, SourceIP=SourceIP, Query=coalesce(RequestURL, DestinationHostName), QueryType="Proxy/FW", Resolved=DestinationIP, Table="CommonSecurityLog")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Rhysida ransomware deployment downstream of SignSpace-signed installer Actions on Objectives High
Detects the impact-phase tail of the OpFauxSign chain: VSS shadow-copy deletion plus Rhysida-style ransom-note artifacts (CriticalBreachDetected.pdf / .rhysida extension family) on a host that recently executed a SignSpace-signed brand-impersonating installer. Anchored on Microsoft's named downstream payload (Rhysida via Vanilla Tempest / Oyster). Rationale: Combines the article's named impact payload (Rhysida via Vanilla Tempest / Oyster) with the SignSpace IOC anchors — the join on host promotes a generic VSS-deletion signal to a high-fidelity per-host correlation. Article cites: 'enabled the deployment of Rhysida ransomware by threat actors such as Vanilla Tempest'. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1486/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1490/ • https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa23-319a
ATT&CKT1486 T1490 T1657
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let SignSpaceSha256 = dynamic(["f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc","11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326","f0a6b89ec7eee83274cd484cea526b970a3ef28038799b0a5774bb33c5793b55"]);
let SignSpaceHosts = union
  (DeviceProcessEvents | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays) | where SHA256 in (SignSpaceSha256) or InitiatingProcessSHA256 in (SignSpaceSha256)),
  (DeviceFileEvents | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays) | where SHA256 in (SignSpaceSha256))
  | summarize SignSpaceFirstSeen = min(Timestamp) by DeviceName;
let RansomActivity = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where (FileName =~ "vssadmin.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "delete" and ProcessCommandLine has "shadows")
     or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "shadowcopy" and ProcessCommandLine has "delete")
     or (FileName =~ "wbadmin.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "delete" and ProcessCommandLine has "catalog")
     or (FileName =~ "bcdedit.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine has "recoveryenabled no" or ProcessCommandLine has "ignoreallfailures"))
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
let RansomNotes = DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where ActionType == "FileCreated"
  | where FileName in~ ("CriticalBreachDetected.pdf","!RhysidaRecovery!.txt","RhysidaReadMe.txt") or FileName endswith ".rhysida"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
union RansomActivity, RansomNotes
| join kind=inner SignSpaceHosts on DeviceName
| where Timestamp > SignSpaceFirstSeen
| extend HoursSinceSignSpace = datetime_diff('hour', Timestamp, SignSpaceFirstSeen)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SignSpaceFirstSeen, HoursSinceSignSpace
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let SignSpaceSha256 = dynamic(["f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc","11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326","f0a6b89ec7eee83274cd484cea526b970a3ef28038799b0a5774bb33c5793b55"]);
let SignSpaceHosts = union
  (ImProcessCreate | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays) | where SHA256 in (SignSpaceSha256)),
  (ImFileEvent | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays) | where TargetFileSHA256 in (SignSpaceSha256))
  | summarize SignSpaceFirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated) by Host = DvcHostname;
let RansomActivity = union isfuzzy=true
  (ImProcessCreate
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)

      or (TargetProcessName has "wmic.exe" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "shadowcopy" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "delete")

   | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, User=ActorUsername, FileName=TargetProcessName, CmdLine=TargetProcessCommandLine, Parent=ParentProcessName),
  (SecurityEvent
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
   | where EventID == 4688
   | where (NewProcessName has "vssadmin.exe" and CommandLine has "delete" and CommandLine has "shadows")
      or (NewProcessName has "wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "shadowcopy" and CommandLine has "delete")
      or (NewProcessName has "wbadmin.exe" and CommandLine has "delete" and CommandLine has "catalog")
      or (NewProcessName has "bcdedit.exe" and (CommandLine has "recoveryenabled no" or CommandLine has "ignoreallfailures"))
   | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, User=Account, FileName=NewProcessName, CmdLine=CommandLine, Parent=ParentProcessName);
let RansomNotes = ImFileEvent

union RansomActivity, RansomNotes
| join kind=inner SignSpaceHosts on Host
| where TimeGenerated > SignSpaceFirstSeen
| extend HoursSinceSignSpace = datetime_diff('hour', TimeGenerated, SignSpaceFirstSeen)
| project TimeGenerated, Host, User, FileName, CmdLine, Parent, SignSpaceFirstSeen, HoursSinceSignSpace
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId
RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Remote-Management (RMM) Tool Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0c
status: experimental
description: |
    AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera / Splashtop /
    RustDesk — RMM tools attackers commonly install for hands-on-

    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:

            - '\TeamViewer.exe'

            - '\atera_agent.exe'
            - '\SplashtopStreamer.exe'

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.

            - '\svchost.exe'

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"

        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents

| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/

date: 2026/05/02

    - attack.t1569.002

    - attack.execution

            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'

ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc", "11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326", "f0a6b89ec7eee83274cd484cea526b970a3ef28038799b0a5774bb33c5793b55", "dc0acb01e3086ea8a9cb144a5f97810d291020ce", "7e6d9dac619c04ae1b3c8c0906123e752ed66d63") or SHA1 in~ ("f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc", "11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326", "f0a6b89ec7eee83274cd484cea526b970a3ef28038799b0a5774bb33c5793b55", "dc0acb01e3086ea8a9cb144a5f97810d291020ce", "7e6d9dac619c04ae1b3c8c0906123e752ed66d63") or MD5 in~ ("f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc", "11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326", "f0a6b89ec7eee83274cd484cea526b970a3ef28038799b0a5774bb33c5793b55", "dc0acb01e3086ea8a9cb144a5f97810d291020ce", "7e6d9dac619c04ae1b3c8c0906123e752ed66d63")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc", "11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326", "f0a6b89ec7eee83274cd484cea526b970a3ef28038799b0a5774bb33c5793b55", "dc0acb01e3086ea8a9cb144a5f97810d291020ce", "7e6d9dac619c04ae1b3c8c0906123e752ed66d63") or SHA1 in~ ("f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc", "11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326", "f0a6b89ec7eee83274cd484cea526b970a3ef28038799b0a5774bb33c5793b55", "dc0acb01e3086ea8a9cb144a5f97810d291020ce", "7e6d9dac619c04ae1b3c8c0906123e752ed66d63") or MD5 in~ ("f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc", "11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326", "f0a6b89ec7eee83274cd484cea526b970a3ef28038799b0a5774bb33c5793b55", "dc0acb01e3086ea8a9cb144a5f97810d291020ce", "7e6d9dac619c04ae1b3c8c0906123e752ed66d63")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc", "11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326", "f0a6b89ec7eee83274cd484cea526b970a3ef28038799b0a5774bb33c5793b55", "dc0acb01e3086ea8a9cb144a5f97810d291020ce", "7e6d9dac619c04ae1b3c8c0906123e752ed66d63"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Webworm Deploys EchoCreep and GraphWorm Backdoors Using Discord and MS Graph API

The Hacker News
2026-05-20 14 use cases 6 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Cybersecurity researchers have flagged fresh activity from a China-aligned threat actor known as Webworm in 2025, deploying custom backdoors that employ Discord and Microsoft Graph API for command-and-control (C2 or C&amp;C) communications. Webworm, first publicly documented by Broadcom-owned Symantec in September 2022, is assessed to be active since at least 2022, targeting government agencies

[LLM] EchoCreep persistence via 'MicrosoftSSHUpdate' scheduled task Installation High
Detects creation of the scheduled task named 'MicrosoftSSHUpdate' that ESET observed EchoCreep dropping for logon persistence. The task name is unique to Webworm's EchoCreep implant and pivots cleanly on schtasks.exe command-line content. Rationale: ESET specifically calls out the scheduled task name 'MicrosoftSSHUpdate' as EchoCreep's persistence mechanism. The string is unique enough that any hit is high-fidelity. Cross-checked welivesecurity.com Webworm research write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/webworm-new-burrowing-techniques/ • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/webworm-apt-evolves-tactics/
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1547.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName =~ "schtasks.exe" or FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe"))
| where ProcessCommandLine has "MicrosoftSSHUpdate"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessSHA256, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID in (4688, 4698)
| where (NewProcessName endswith "\\schtasks.exe" or CommandLine has_any ("schtasks","Register-ScheduledTask"))
| where CommandLine has "MicrosoftSSHUpdate" or EventData has "MicrosoftSSHUpdate"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, EventID
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Webworm EchoCreep MicrosoftSSHUpdate Scheduled Task Persistence
id: b3f2a1c8-7d4e-4f6b-9e8a-1c2d3e4f5a6b
description: Detects creation of the 'MicrosoftSSHUpdate' scheduled task used by Webworm's EchoCreep Discord backdoor for logon persistence.
references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/webworm-new-burrowing-techniques/
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/webworm-deploys-echocreep-and-graphworm.html

date: 2026/05/20

logsource:

detection:

  condition: all of selection_*

(source:windows.security OR source:windows.sysmon) (@EventID:(4688 OR 4698 OR 1)) (@Image:(*\\schtasks.exe OR *\\Schtasks.exe OR *\\SCHTASKS.EXE OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe) OR @NewProcessName:(*\\schtasks.exe OR *\\Schtasks.exe OR *\\SCHTASKS.EXE)) @CommandLine:*MicrosoftSSHUpdate*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\(schtasks|powershell|pwsh|cmd)\.exe$/i
| regex("MicrosoftSSHUpdate", field=CommandLine, flags="i")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="schtasks.exe" OR Processes.process_name="powershell.exe" OR Processes.process_name="pwsh.exe") Processes.process="*MicrosoftSSHUpdate*" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(user, "\$$") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] GraphWorm OneDrive Microsoft Graph API C2 from non-Office process Command & Control Medium
Detects connections to graph.microsoft.com originating from a process that is neither an Office client nor the OneDrive sync agent. GraphWorm exclusively uses OneDrive Graph endpoints (/me/drive/...) for jobs and result upload, so unusual parent processes hitting graph.microsoft.com are a strong C2 signal. Rationale: ESET states GraphWorm 'uses OneDrive endpoints exclusively' via Microsoft Graph; the detection looks for graph.microsoft.com traffic originating from binaries that are NOT Office / OneDrive / browser. AES-256-CBC + base64 encoding noted but not used as a query primitive (TLS hides body). Cross-checked welivesecurity.com and gbhackers.com. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/webworm-new-burrowing-techniques/ • https://gbhackers.com/graphworm-malware-abuses-microsoft-onedrive/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/graphworm-malware-uses-microsoft-onedrive/
ATT&CKT1102.002 T1567.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let OfficeStack = dynamic(["onedrive.exe","outlook.exe","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","onenote.exe","teams.exe","ms-teams.exe","msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","msoia.exe","officeclicktorun.exe","searchapp.exe","searchindexer.exe","explorer.exe","backgroundtaskhost.exe","runtimebroker.exe","olk.exe","sharepoint.exe","msaccess.exe","microsoftedgeupdate.exe"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "graph.microsoft.com"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ (OfficeStack)
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft Office\\"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft Office\\"
| summarize ConnCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Urls = make_set(RemoteUrl, 5) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessSHA256, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by ConnCount desc
let OfficeStack = dynamic(["onedrive.exe","outlook.exe","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","onenote.exe","teams.exe","msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","msoia.exe","officeclicktorun.exe"]);
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Url has "graph.microsoft.com" or HttpHostName =~ "graph.microsoft.com"
| extend ProcName = tolower(tostring(split(FileName,"\\")[-1]))
| where ProcName !in (OfficeStack) and isnotempty(ProcName)
| summarize ConnCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Urls = make_set(Url, 5) by DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, ProcName
| order by ConnCount desc
title: GraphWorm Microsoft Graph API C2 From Non-Office Process

[LLM] EchoCreep Discord API C2 channel from non-browser, non-Discord process Command & Control Medium
Detects discord.com / discordapp.com connections from processes that are not Discord, Update.exe, or known browsers. ESET decrypted 433 messages flowing through Discord channels named after victim IPs — Webworm's EchoCreep is the article-specific use case. Rationale: ESET decrypted 433 Discord C2 messages tied to victim-IP-named channels — the highest-fidelity pivot is 'Discord API endpoint reached from a process that is NOT the Discord client / browser / Slack-Discord bridge'. The filename of EchoCreep is unknown, so we hunt by anomaly. Corroborated by welivesecurity.com and thehackernews.com. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/webworm-new-burrowing-techniques/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/webworm-deploys-echocreep-and-graphworm.html
ATT&CKT1102.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let BrowserOrDiscord = dynamic(["discord.exe","update.exe","discordcanary.exe","discordptb.exe","msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","vivaldi.exe","slack.exe","msteams.exe","teams.exe"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("discord.com","discordapp.com","cdn.discordapp.com","discord-cdn.com","discord.media")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ (BrowserOrDiscord)
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\Users\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath !contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Discord\\"
| summarize ConnCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Urls = make_set(RemoteUrl, 5), Ports = make_set(RemotePort, 5) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessSHA256, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by ConnCount desc
let BrowserOrDiscord = dynamic(["discord.exe","update.exe","discordcanary.exe","msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","slack.exe","teams.exe"]);
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where Url has_any ("discord.com","discordapp.com","cdn.discordapp.com","discord-cdn.com")
   or HttpHostName has_any ("discord.com","discordapp.com")
| extend ProcName = tolower(tostring(split(FileName,"\\")[-1]))
| where ProcName !in (BrowserOrDiscord) and isnotempty(ProcName)
| summarize ConnCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Urls = make_set(Url, 5) by DvcHostname, SrcUsername, ProcName
| order by ConnCount desc

[LLM] Webworm GitHub staging repo access (anjsdgasdf/WordPress) Delivery High
Detects any HTTPS access or git clone to github.com/anjsdgasdf/WordPress, the WordPress-fork-impersonating repository Webworm uses as a malware/SoftEther staging ground. Hits on this URL pattern are essentially zero-FP. Rationale: github.com/anjsdgasdf/WordPress is explicitly called out as the Webworm staging URL. The username slug 'anjsdgasdf' is unique and very unlikely to appear in a benign analyst environment. Confirmed in welivesecurity.com and thehackernews.com. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/webworm-new-burrowing-techniques/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/webworm-deploys-echocreep-and-graphworm.html
ATT&CKT1105 T1608.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(180d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("anjsdgasdf/WordPress","github.com/anjsdgasdf","raw.githubusercontent.com/anjsdgasdf","codeload.github.com/anjsdgasdf")
   or RemoteUrl has "anjsdgasdf"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(
  ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(180d)
  | where Url has_any ("anjsdgasdf/WordPress","github.com/anjsdgasdf","raw.githubusercontent.com/anjsdgasdf","codeload.github.com/anjsdgasdf")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Url, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
),
(
  CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(180d)
  | where RequestURL has_any ("anjsdgasdf/WordPress","github.com/anjsdgasdf","raw.githubusercontent.com/anjsdgasdf")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=SourceHostName, SrcIpAddr=SourceIP, SrcUsername=SourceUserName, Url=RequestURL, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent=RequestClientApplication
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] GraphWorm beacon_shell_output.txt artifact on disk Actions on Objectives High
Detects creation, write, or rename of files named 'beacon_shell_output.txt' — the temporary file GraphWorm uses to stage shell command output before uploading to OneDrive and deleting locally. The exact filename is unique to GraphWorm. Rationale: ESET documents that GraphWorm 'removes beacon_shell_output.txt after uploading' the shell result — the literal filename string is unique enough to alert on directly. Corroborated via welivesecurity.com and cybersecuritynews.com. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/webworm-new-burrowing-techniques/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/graphworm-malware-uses-microsoft-onedrive/
ATT&CKT1059.003 T1074.001 T1567.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where FileName =~ "beacon_shell_output.txt" or PreviousFileName =~ "beacon_shell_output.txt"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, PreviousFolderPath, PreviousFileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessSHA256, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "beacon_shell_output.txt" or TargetFilePath has "beacon_shell_output.txt"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Webworm C2 IP connection on Vultr/IT7 infrastructure Command & Control High
Detects any outbound connection from corporate endpoints to the five known Webworm C2 IPs hosted on Vultr (45.77.13.67, 64.176.85.158, 108.61.200.151) and IT7 Networks (104.243.23.43, 144.168.60.233). Direct IOC match — alert on first hit. Rationale: Five Webworm C2 IPs published in the article with ASN-level corroboration (Vultr / IT7 Networks) via ESET; SHA1 hashes also added to the Defender query as a secondary file-level pivot. IOC match is binary — any hit warrants immediate triage. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/webworm-new-burrowing-techniques/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/webworm-deploys-echocreep-and-graphworm.html • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/webworm-apt-evolves-tactics/

(

  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,

),
(

[LLM] WormFrp configuration retrieval from compromised Amazon S3 bucket Command & Control High
Detects HTTP(S) access to wamanharipethe.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com — the compromised S3 bucket Webworm uses to host WormFrp configuration files and stage exfiltrated Spanish government data. Direct IOC, zero-FP outside research environments. Rationale: ESET specifically names 'wamanharipethe.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com' as the compromised S3 bucket WormFrp retrieves config from and where exfiltrated Spanish-government data was found. The substring 'wamanharipethe' is unique and zero-FP outside research. Corroborated via welivesecurity.com. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/webworm-new-burrowing-techniques/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/webworm-deploys-echocreep-and-graphworm.html

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2017-7692")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2017-7692")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,

// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9") or SHA1 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9") or MD5 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9") or SHA1 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9") or MD5 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

2026-05-20 8 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Microsoft on Tuesday released a mitigation for a BitLocker bypass vulnerability named YellowKey following its public disclosure last week. The zero-day flaw, now tracked as CVE-2026-45585, carries a CVSS score of 6.8. It has been described as a BitLocker security feature bypass. Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] YellowKey CVE-2026-45585 unmitigated state — autofstx.exe still in WinRE BootExecute · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Agent AI is Coming. Are You Ready?
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] YellowKey mitigation tampered — autofstx.exe re-added to WinRE BootExecute REG_MULTI_SZ
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] YellowKey CVE-2026-45585 unmitigated state — autofstx.exe still in WinRE BootExecute Exploitation High
Compliance hunt for Windows 11 24H2/25H2/26H1 and Server 2025 hosts where the most recent observed Session Manager\BootExecute REG_MULTI_SZ still contains autofstx.exe. Per Microsoft's mitigation, the FsTx Auto Recovery Utility (autofstx.exe) must be removed from BootExecute on the WinRE image; any device whose latest registry state still references autofstx is vulnerable to the YellowKey BitLocker bypass via WinRE. Rationale: Targets the exact registry artifact named in Microsoft's mitigation guidance and Will Dormann's analysis (quoted in the article): autofstx.exe value inside HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\BootExecute. Uses arg_max per-device to surface latest observed state, so devices whose mitigation has been correctly applied (autofstx removed) drop out of results. High-fidelity because the affected registry value is small, well-defined, and the binary name autofstx.exe is article-specific (FsTx Auto Recovery Utility).
ATT&CKT1542.003 T1112
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where RegistryKey endswith @"Control\Session Manager"
| where RegistryValueName =~ "BootExecute"
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by DeviceId
| where RegistryValueData has "autofstx"
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceInfo
    | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, OSPlatform, OSVersion, OSBuild) by DeviceId
  ) on DeviceId
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSVersion, OSBuild,
          RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where RegistryKey endswith @"Control\Session Manager"
| where RegistryValue =~ "BootExecute"
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by DvcHostname
| where RegistryValueData has "autofstx"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData,
          ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: YellowKey CVE-2026-45585 Unmitigated - autofstx.exe Present in WinRE BootExecute
id: 4b8e1f3d-c2a4-4f8b-9d7c-8e3f1a2b5c6d
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects Windows hosts where Session Manager\BootExecute registry value still references autofstx.exe, indicating Microsoft's mitigation for CVE-2026-45585 (YellowKey BitLocker bypass) has not been applied to the WinRE image on this device.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/agent-ai-is-coming-are-you-ready.html
  - https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-45585
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1542.003
  - attack.t1112
logsource:
  category: registry_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetObject|endswith: '\Control\Session Manager\BootExecute'
    Details|contains: 'autofstx'
  condition: selection
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:13 @TargetObject:(*\\Control\\Session\ Manager\\BootExecute OR *\\control\\session\ manager\\bootexecute) @Details:(*autofstx* OR *AutoFstx* OR *AUTOFSTX*)
#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate
| RegObjectName=/\\Session Manager$/i
| RegValueName=/^BootExecute$/i
| RegStringValue=/autofstx/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName], function={ max(@timestamp, as=lastSeen) | collect([RegStringValue, ContextImageFileName]) })
| sort(lastSeen, order=desc)

[LLM] YellowKey mitigation tampered — autofstx.exe re-added to WinRE BootExecute REG_MULTI_SZ Installation High
Detects a new write to Session Manager\BootExecute that introduces autofstx.exe back into the REG_MULTI_SZ value AFTER it was previously absent. Post-mitigation for CVE-2026-45585, this transition is never expected from legitimate Windows servicing; it indicates either deliberate rollback (change-managed) or an adversary restoring the vulnerable WinRE state to enable physical-access BitLocker bypass. Rationale: Combines the article's exact mitigation artifact (autofstx.exe in Session Manager\BootExecute REG_MULTI_SZ, per Will Dormann's quoted guidance) with a state-transition predicate: previous value absent autofstx, new value contains it. That delta is never produced by routine Windows servicing post-mitigation — only by deliberate rollback or attacker tampering — making this a high-confidence, low-FP alerting signal. Differs from UC1 (state hunt across fleet) by targeting the moment-of-tampering rather than current posture.
ATT&CKT1112 T1542.003 T1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet", "RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey endswith @"Control\Session Manager"
| where RegistryValueName =~ "BootExecute"
| where RegistryValueData has "autofstx"
| where isnotempty(PreviousRegistryValueData) and not (PreviousRegistryValueData has "autofstx")
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName,
          PreviousRegistryValueData, RegistryValueData,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountDomain, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RegistryKey endswith @"Control\Session Manager"
| where RegistryValue =~ "BootExecute"
| where RegistryValueData has "autofstx"
| where isnotempty(RegistryPreviousValueData) and not (RegistryPreviousValueData has "autofstx")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname,
          RegistryKey, RegistryValue,
          RegistryPreviousValueData, RegistryValueData,
          ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: YellowKey Mitigation Tampering - autofstx.exe Re-added to Session Manager BootExecute
id: 7d2e8f4a-1b3c-4a5d-8e6f-9c2b3d4e5f6a
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects re-introduction of autofstx.exe into the Session Manager\BootExecute REG_MULTI_SZ registry value after Microsoft's CVE-2026-45585 (YellowKey BitLocker bypass) mitigation has been applied. Restoring autofstx to BootExecute re-enables the Transactional NTFS replay that deletes winpeshl.ini and exposes the host to the WinRE pre-boot shell bypass.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/agent-ai-is-coming-are-you-ready.html
  - https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-45585
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1112
  - attack.t1542.003
  - attack.t1562.001
logsource:
  category: registry_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    EventType: SetValue
    TargetObject|endswith: '\Control\Session Manager\BootExecute'
    Details|contains: 'autofstx'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:13 @TargetObject:(*\\Control\\Session\ Manager\\BootExecute OR *\\control\\session\ manager\\bootexecute) @Details:(*autofstx* OR *AutoFstx* OR *AUTOFSTX*) -@Image:(*\\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\\trustedinstaller.exe)
#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate
| RegObjectName=/\\Session Manager$/i
| RegValueName=/^BootExecute$/i
| RegStringValue=/autofstx/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RegStringValue], function={ min(@timestamp, as=firstSeen) | max(@timestamp, as=lastSeen) | count(as=writes) })
| sort(lastSeen, order=desc)

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45585")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,

// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45585")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc
